messages:
maya: Heads-up: large jump in Pending GPU pods in ap-southeast1c starting ~05:03 UTC. Lots of tiny allocations getting evicted repeatedly. Spotted ~120 pending, eviction spikes in metrics. cc @devin @pavel

devin: Looking. Cluster events show a taint `gpu-maint:NoSchedule` applied to four nodes in rack ap-southeast1c at 05:00. That lines up with a scheduled maintenance job but I thought the job targeted ap-southeast1b only.

pavel: I kicked off the taint rollout yesterday for ap-southeast1b. The label-sync batch may have expanded the target set after a rack-label normalization. I see a `labels-syncer` run at 04:58 that touched rack metadata across the region.

maya: The core issue: fragmentation + churn. Tiny pods (0.1-0.25 GPU) are spread across many nodes; once tainted they get evicted and scatter into the pending queue. Autoscaler keeps spinning warm nodes to replace them which then get re-evicted -> cost and scheduling thrash.

infra-sre: Cost note: warm node churn is adding ~2.8 GPU-hours over last 30m. Warm spin cold-start ~5-6m. If this continues we'll exceed the daily ops budget.

leyla: Before we do any mass rollback, what's the maintenance intent? If nodes were flagged for driver updates we shouldn't untaint blindly. Any kernel/driver alerts tied to those nodes?

devin: No active kernel faults in monitoring for those nodes. The maintenance run appears to be an automated taint step from the maintenance orchestration but it seems to have run without the usual canary checks.

pavel: Oof. The syncer expanded the rack label set because of an upstream mapping change. I think the rollout selector accidentally matched ap-southeast1c. I'll take ownership to audit and mitigate.

maya: Proposed actions: 1) temporarily remove the taint on the 4 nodes to stop immediate evictions, 2) pause autoscaler for the region to avoid thundering, 3) add a quick guard to the maintenance job to check pending GPU < 20 and eviction_rate < 1/min before tainting. Thoughts?

infra-sre: Sounds good. We can also crank the warm pool +2 for 10m to buffer while we debug, but that costs ~ $4/hr. Given current burn, rollback + pause autoscaler is cheaper short-term.

devin: I'll remove the taint on the affected nodes and tail eviction controller and kubelet logs. Command:

```
kubectl taint node node-apse1c-r02 gpu-maint:NoSchedule-  # remove taint
kubectl taint node node-apse1c-r03 gpu-maint:NoSchedule-
kubectl taint node node-apse1c-r04 gpu-maint:NoSchedule-
kubectl taint node node-apse1c-r05 gpu-maint:NoSchedule-
```

I'll then re-run the maintenance with a safer canary check after we fix the syncer mapping.

maya: Removing taints now. Pausing autoscaler for ap-southeast1 region.

ops-bot: Incident bot: Eviction surge (ap-southeast1 GPU) acknowledged by devin at 05:12 UTC. Autoscaler paused for ap-southeast1.

maya: After removing taints, pending started decreasing; about 65 of the 120 cleared in the first 2 minutes. Eviction rate dropped from ~8/min -> ~0.5/min.

pavel: I'll open a PR to add a label-blacklist to the syncer and a canary gate on maintenance that verifies cluster packing metrics and pending/gpu count. Also adding an operator warning if a taint would hit racks with >50% fragmentation.

leyla: Can we add an alert that triggers when warm pool scale events lead to >1.5x baseline for more than 10m? That would help cost ops catch regressive behavior early.

infra-sre: Will add a small runbook: rollback taint -> pause autoscaler -> safe-reapply via canary script -> verify pending/evict metrics. I'll include cost delta numbers.

devin: Leaving autoscaler paused until we confirm steady state for 15m. If eviction spikes again i'll escalate to eng-oncall.

maya: Thanks. Post-incident follow-ups: fix syncer mapping, add canary checks to maint job, add fragmentation-aware taint blacklist, and add cost-hedge alert.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: Eviction rate normalized. Incident logged as 2026-03-23-apse1c-taint-mismatch. :white_check_mark:
